Specify a SAOM from a formula written for any model

Source: R/specify_formula.R, R/specify_report.R
specify_saom.Rd

specify_saom() reads a formula, whichever model it was written for, and writes each term as the {RSiena} effect of a stochastic actor-oriented model (SAOM). With the network, it returns the sienaEffects object that RSiena::siena() fits, with the sienadata object it is for. specify_mrqap() and specify_ergm() read the same formulas for their models, and also read a sienaEffects object.

A term with an equivalent in RSiena is rewritten as that effect. A term RSiena cannot fit is dropped and named, so that the rest of the model still fits. Rewritten terms are reported with manynet::snet_info(), which is silent unless options(snet_verbosity = "verbose"), and dropped terms are reported in one warning.

Usage

specify_saom(formula, .data = NULL, input = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'saom_formula'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

formula

A formula written for an MRQAP, goldfish, ergm, or RSiena, a list of such formulas, one for each dependent network, or a sienaEffects object. Without it, or with . as its right-hand side, the table of every term for .data, as specify_terms describes, with the RSiena effect of each in its column as.

.data

Optionally, the network the formula is for, with at least two waves. With it, the result is a sienaEffects object, which needs {RSiena}. Without it, the result is a formula, and RSiena is not needed.

input

The model the formula was written for: "mrqap", "dynam", "rem", "ergm", or "saom". NULL, the default, reads it from the class of the formula, such as goldfish's "goldfishFormula", or else from the names in the formula.

object

A formula returned by specify_saom().

...

Not used.

Value

Without .data, a formula of class c("saom_formula", "formula"), or a list of them. Its input attribute names the model it was read from, and its record attribute holds what RSiena makes of each term. summary() returns every term as a tibble, with the columns term, status, as, and reason.

With .data, the sienaEffects object of RSiena::getEffects(), with the effects of the formula included. Its attribute data holds the sienadata object, formula the SAOM formula, or the list of them, and record what RSiena makes of each term.

Without a formula, the table of every term for .data, as specify_terms describes.

Writing a formula for RSiena

Each effect is written as its RSiena short name, with the covariate or network it reads as its argument: ego(sex) is egoX(sex), same(sex) is sameX(sex), diff(age) is absDiffX(age), a layer such as primary is X(primary), and trans is transTrip. terms_mrqap gives the effect for each term. A formula written in RSiena's short names, such as friends ~ recip + transTrip + inPop + egoX(sex), is read as one written for RSiena, and an effect that has no equivalent in the other models, such as inPop, is kept as it is. density is always added, as the outdegree effect that every SAOM of a network has. Every other evaluation effect is in the model only if the formula names it: recip, which RSiena includes by default, is left out where the formula does not name it, and a message says so. A random intercept, a fixed effect, a reporter term, global(), and (for now) an interaction are dropped. Add an interaction to the result with RSiena::includeInteraction().

The data and the dependent variables

With .data, the network is coerced with manynet::as_siena(). The left-hand side of the formula names the dependent network, which must be a layer of the network, or . for its focal layer. A list of formulas names several dependent networks, one for each formula. Only these layers are dependent variables: every other layer becomes a dyadic covariate, and every node attribute a covariate, constant or changing across the waves. A dependent behaviour is not yet written here; for one, build the effects with RSiena::getEffects(). Each effect is checked against the effects that RSiena has for the data, and a name that it does not have aborts with the nearest name. The model is then fitted with RSiena::siena() of the data and the effects, as in the last example. siena() writes an output file in the working directory, named after its data argument, unless control_out = RSiena::set_output_saom(outputName = ) names another.

What each model makes of each term

summary() of the result has one row for each term of the formula, and fits nothing. Its status is what the model makes of the term:

  • "fits": the model fits the term as it is written;

  • "adapted": the term is rewritten as its equivalent in the model, in as;

  • "interpreted": the model has a term of the same name that it defines differently, as reason says;

  • "warns": the model fits the term, but with a warning, as reason says;

  • "drops": the model cannot fit the term, so it is left out, and the rest is fitted;

  • "refuses": the model aborts, as reason says.

An MRQAP warns for a term that reads the outcome's own ties, such as recip, and refuses tie(), indeg(), and outdeg() of the outcome layer. It drops an offset, such as goldfish's offset(recip, coef = 0), since it estimates every coefficient; ergm keeps an ergm one. For an MRQAP, summary() with .data also builds each term and names its columns, as estimate_mrqap() names them.

Reading the model a formula was written for

The model a formula was written for is read, in order, from input, from the class of the formula, such as "ergm_formula", or from the names in the formula:

  • "ergm" where a term is named only in ergm, such as edges, mutual, or nodematch("x");

  • "saom" where an effect is named only in RSiena, such as transTrip, inPop, or egoX(sex);

  • "dynam" where a term is named only in goldfish, such as inertia or trans;

  • "mrqap" otherwise.

A sienaEffects object of {RSiena} is read as the formula of the evaluation effects it includes for its first dependent network.

The model that was read is reported. Where a formula mixes ergm's names with goldfish's, it is read as an ergm formula, and goldfish's names in it are read as they are in goldfish. The result of each function carries its model as its class, so that specify_ergm(specify_mrqap(f)) reads its input without a guess.

See also

terms_mrqap for the RSiena effect of each term, and specify_terms for the terms that suit a network.

Other specifying functions: declare_coefs(), declare_coefs_ergm, specify_ergm(), specify_mrqap(), specify_terms, terms_mrqap

Examples

# An MRQAP formula, written for RSiena
specify_saom(friends ~ recip + trans + ego(sex) + same(sex) + primary)
#> # A SAOM formula read from a formula for goldfish
#> 
#> friends ~ density + recip + transTrip + egoX(sex) + sameX(sex) + 
#>     X(primary)
#> 
#> # adapted trans -> transTrip
#> # adapted ego(sex) -> egoX(sex)
#> # adapted same(sex) -> sameX(sex)
#> # adapted primary -> X(primary)
# The terms that RSiena can take for a network
specify_saom(friends ~ ., manynet::ison_classmates)
#> 30 terms for RSiena of friends
#> # A tibble: 30 × 5
#>    term                                         effect     layer attribute as   
#>    <chr>                                        <chr>      <chr> <chr>     <chr>
#>  1 ego(sex)                                     ego        NA    sex       egoX…
#>  2 alter(sex)                                   alter      NA    sex       altX…
#>  3 same(sex)                                    same       NA    sex       same…
#>  4 ego(age)                                     ego        NA    age       egoX…
#>  5 alter(age)                                   alter      NA    age       altX…
#>  6 diff(age)                                    diff       NA    age       absD…
#>  7 diff(age, transformer_fn = identity)         diff       NA    age       diff…
#>  8 sim(age)                                     sim        NA    age       simX…
#>  9 ego(ethnicity)                               ego        NA    ethnicity egoX…
#> 10 alter(ethnicity)                             alter      NA    ethnicity altX…
#> 11 same(ethnicity)                              same       NA    ethnicity same…
#> 12 ego(religion)                                ego        NA    religion  egoX…
#> 13 alter(religion)                              alter      NA    religion  altX…
#> 14 same(religion)                               same       NA    religion  same…
#> 15 ego(delinquency)                             ego        NA    delinque… egoX…
#> 16 alter(delinquency)                           alter      NA    delinque… altX…
#> 17 diff(delinquency)                            diff       NA    delinque… absD…
#> 18 diff(delinquency, transformer_fn = identity) diff       NA    delinque… diff…
#> 19 sim(delinquency)                             sim        NA    delinque… simX…
#> 20 indeg(friends)                               indeg      frie… NA        inPop
#> 21 indeg(friends, node = 'ego')                 indeg      frie… NA        inAct
#> 22 outdeg(friends)                              outdeg     frie… NA        outA…
#> 23 outdeg(friends, node = 'alter')              outdeg     frie… NA        outP…
#> 24 tie(primary)                                 tie        prim… NA        X(pr…
#> 25 recip                                        recip      NA    NA        recip
#> 26 trans                                        trans      NA    NA        tran…
#> 27 cycle                                        cycle      NA    NA        cycl…
#> 28 common_sender                                common_se… NA    NA        gwes…
#> 29 common_receiver                              common_re… NA    NA        gwes…
#> 30 four                                         four       NA    NA        cycl…
#> Choose rows, and `formula()` of them gives their formula.
# The effects object that RSiena::siena() fits
eff <- specify_saom(friends ~ recip + trans + ego(sex) + same(sex),
                    manynet::ison_classmates)
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
data <- attr(eff, "data")
# \donttest{
fit <- RSiena::siena(data, eff, batch = TRUE, silent = TRUE,
  control_algo = RSiena::set_algorithm_saom(nsub = 1, n3 = 50, seed = 1),
  control_out = RSiena::set_output_saom(outputName = file.path(tempdir(), "classmates")))
# }
summary(specify_saom(friends ~ recip + trans + ego(sex) + tie(primary)))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   term         status  as         reason
#>   <chr>        <chr>   <chr>      <chr> 
#> 1 recip        fits    recip      NA    
#> 2 trans        adapted transTrip  NA    
#> 3 ego(sex)     adapted egoX(sex)  NA    
#> 4 tie(primary) adapted X(primary) NA
